title: integrate: four operational failures are raised as merge refusals
description:
From the qeu final review (gcx), wave 11 review pass. Pre-existing; entrenched
rather than introduced by wave 11.

Four of integrate.go's RefusedMerge sites are not verdicts about the attempt at
all — they are operational failures of this host or this network:

- integrate.go:49  durableAttemptHead could not make the collected head durable
- integrate.go:52  fetch of the attempt branch from the remote failed
- integrate.go:55  the head is not a commit this checkout has
- integrate.go:99  the integration branch moved under this reconciler N times
                   running, whose own message says "that is an operational
                   problem, not a conflict to spin on"

This contradicts the doctrine disposeRefused states in its own comment: "Only a
REFUSAL tears anything down. An operational error — an unreachable remote, a
tracker that would not answer — is not a verdict on the attempt, and a run that
disposed of an attempt over one would be throwing work away because a network
was down."

Because they are refusals, the run loop marks the tick rejected and checkpoints
it, and the attempt is torn down. So a network blip or lease contention now
costs a human `ticfac settle --release` before the epic can move, and the same
blip during the settle guard's own read is refused a second time.

The repair is a vocabulary one: these four should be operational errors returned
as-is (the push path at integrate.go already does exactly this for a push that
is not a lease race, and says why), leaving only the genuine conflict — the
merge that does not apply — as RefusedMerge. Check every caller's error handling
before changing the class: processTick returns the error either way, but only a
refusal reaches disposeRefused and the run loop's rejection.
acceptance_criteria: A failed fetch, an unmakeable durable head, an absent commit and lease exhaustion are returned as operational errors rather than RefusedMerge, so they do not reject the tick, do not tear the attempt down, and do not need a human settle; a genuine merge conflict still refuses as RefusedMerge; tests cover an operational failure leaving the attempt adoptable and a conflict still refusing.
